findings.finding: The Phase-2 premise that the fix 'fits the existing default budget of four model-request steps per criterion (three evidence steps plus the record transition)' is a specific per-criterion quantitative claim that the code does not literally establish: the budget model computes a per-RUN request budget N = ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2) from a criteria-scaled floor (completion_banking.py:197-216 plan_recovery_pool / verify_step_floor), not an explicit 4-steps-per-criterion allocation. If the true effective budget is fewer than ~4 requests per criterion for the trigger fixture (>=3 dense criteria), the prescribed 'at most three additional evidence-tool calls then record' loop may not actually fit, undermining the Phase-2 mechanism.
findings.location: Phase 2 repair plan > Mechanism and minimal repair, item 3-4 ('fits the existing default budget of four model-request steps per criterion')
scenarios: A >=3-criterion graph=True epic where the criteria-scaled floor yields fewer than ~4 model requests per criterion, so the affirmative bounded loop cannot complete evidence+bank for every id within budget

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Demonstrate that the primary per-run request budget (ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2)) accommodates the bounded 4-step-per-criterion loop across the criteria-count range, or state how the loop degrades gracefully when per-criterion budget falls below the 3-evidence+1-record bound.
evidence: Plan: 'fits the existing default budget of four model-request steps per criterion (three evidence steps plus the record transition)'
completion_banking.py:197-216 plan_recovery_pool: per-run request budget N = ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2); floor scales with criteria count c (e.g. c=8 → floor 64, N 32)
cf3c observed: req_limit=24 for 4 ACs ≈ 6 req/criterion (fits), but the general fit across c is not demonstrated in the plan
findings.finding: The Phase 2 mechanism claims a bounded per-criterion loop (three evidence calls + one record call = four model-request steps per criterion) 'fits the existing default budget of four model-request steps per criterion,' but does not show that the primary's per-run request budget — derived as ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2) which scales with criteria count — actually accommodates a 4-step-per-criterion loop across the criteria-count range. If the derived budget yields fewer than ~4 requests per criterion for larger c, the affirmative loop would itself exhaust before banking later criteria, partially reproducing the original defect.
findings.location: Phase 2 repair plan → 'Mechanism and minimal repair', item 3-4 ('fits the existing default budget of four model-request steps per criterion')
scenarios: A dense epic with many criteria where verify_step_floor/2 divided across criteria yields <4 requests/criterion, so the bounded loop runs out before banking the tail criteria
findings.suggested_fix: Add the budget arithmetic to the plan: for representative c values, show requests-per-criterion = ceil(verify_step_floor(c)/2)/c and confirm it stays >= the loop's per-criterion step bound (or specify that the loop caps evidence calls dynamically to fit remaining budget, banking met=false when starved).
